audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows disagree with the packet and with the mirror, which already flipped win[0], win[3], win[4] to Fiora and win[6] to Skill. The page also grades a 47.06% matchup where Fiora owns six of seven stages as 'Tricky'.
audit.why: Both layers agreed with each other and both disagreed with the mirror, so the two directions of this matchup render opposite answers on four rows.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Fiora on rows 0-5 and Skill at 2+ items as matched full/content pairs; diff HARD, carryRating 8/10, tone to the hard colour, both difficulty lines rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0] through phases[6] carried boilerplate naming no Fiora ability and describing a Stormsurge spike the content layer does not build.
audit.why: The timeline is Lunge from level 1, Riposte from level 2, and a level-6 window that only exists while Riposte's 24 seconds are down.
audit.corrected: All seven rewritten on Lunge, Riposte's 24s, the Vitals and the disguised Pop Blossom.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4], spikes[1], mid and wants.you[1] all say to ult 'from a Shapesplitter clone or invis'. Neeko's W has no invisibility. spikes[3] refers to 'the W shield/clone' and late to being squishy 'after W and shields' — she has no shield either. Riposte's actual rule was stated loosely: it stuns only if it blocked an immobilizing effect, and it is 24/22/20/18/16s.
audit.why: The reason the level-6 ult works is Inherent Glamour: Riot's text says Pop Blossom's preparation is hidden while Neeko is disguised, so a disguised ult is the version she cannot pre-parry. And leading with the root is exactly what upgrades her stab into a stun.
audit.corrected: Invisibility and shield claims replaced with the disguise and the clone; report[5].t rebuilt on the 24s and the blocked-immobilize rule; dontsFull[0].d now states that Lunge applies on-hit effects.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' after Riposte.
audit.why: Riposte is 24 seconds at rank 1 — a far bigger window than the page claimed, and the one the whole all-in plan hangs on.
audit.corrected: 24s written into dosFull[2].d, report[5].t and spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer is written in the first person ('I have no combo', 'she just walks me down') while the rest of the file and the approved bar use second person; the full layer separately calls Fiora 'he'.
audit.why: Voice inconsistency inside one matchup page.
audit.corrected: whys, early, mid and late converted to second person; Fiora's pronouns fixed in the full-layer strings edited here.

edits.before: Through 4-5 I'm shoving with Q waveclear and pretending to be even — I will not all-in a duelist without my ult. If I show the ult, she just W's the slam and stuns me out of it. Land E first, then Q, then drop on her — or don't commit at all and roam to a winning lane instead.

Level 6 is your one real window: Pop Blossom turns a landed E into a burst-and-stun combo, and the version that works is ulting while disguised, because Inherent Glamour hides the preparation she would otherwise pre-parry. Show the ult openly and she simply Ripostes the slam. Land E first, then Q, then drop on her — or don't commit at all and roam to a winning lane instead.

edits.before: Long-term this is her duel, not mine. I survive by being a teamfight bomb, not a splitpush answer — I never 1v1 her for a side wave. Group, save Pop Blossom for her engage onto my carries, and let my team trade the map while I delete the clustered fight.

notes: Same two fabrications as the rest of the slice — Shapesplitter 'invis' in four fields and a Neeko 'shield' in two — and here they were load-bearing, because the whole level-6 plan was built on ulting from invisibility. The real mechanic is Inherent Glamour hiding Pop Blossom's preparation while disguised. Riposte's rule was also stated loosely: it stuns only when it has blocked an immobilizing effect, which is precisely why leading with Tangle-Barbs is the losing sequence, and it is 24 seconds at rank 1 rather than the 'fifteen' the page claimed. Four chart rows disagreed with the mirror's already-published flips. The content layer was written in first person throughout and is converted to second person here.
